title: Procurement, China
leads: Nobody. You look after the suppliers who make our phones, mounts, caps, and chargers.
where: China, or remote and working with Chinese suppliers every day
hours: Daytime, on China time. Reachable while an order is on its way
summary: You buy the phones and the gear on every worker's head, in large numbers, on time.

posting.headline: Procurement, China (phones and collection hardware)
posting.about: We run video recording teams at factories, warehouses, farms, and construction sites across Cairo. Workers wear a small camera on a cap while they do their normal job. Every worker wears a phone, a mount, and a cap, and every ten phones need chargers and spares. You buy all of it in China, in large numbers, and get it to Egypt on time.
do: Buy phones, mounts, caps, chargers, and cables in large numbers.
Find suppliers, compare them, and keep the good ones.
Agree the price and the delivery date before any order is placed.
Check a sample before every large order. Send photos to the Hardware Design Engineer.
Track every order from the factory to Cairo. Say early when a date will slip.
Keep the spare pool full: ten percent extra of every item.
Work with the Head of Deployment on what Egypt needs next, and by when.
need: You have bought goods from Chinese factories before, in large numbers.
You speak and write Chinese, and you can write plain English.
Careful with a list. Every unit, every price, every date.
Honest with numbers. You report a bad sample or a late date the same day.
plus: You have bought smartphones or phone accessories before.
You have visited a factory and checked a production line yourself.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
A weekly call with the CPO, who owns the hardware.
A clear job: the right gear, at the right price, on time.
Your work on the head of every worker we film.
posting.apply: Send your name, where you live, a phone number, and one product you have bought in large numbers. We call back within two working days.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of Procurement, China at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the CPO.
Your start date is {start}. Your first month is with {manager}: the item list, the suppliers we use today, and your first sample check.

terms.label: Place of work
terms.v: China, or remote and working with Chinese suppliers every day

terms.label: Hours
terms.v: Daytime, on China time. Reachable while an order is on its way

terms.label: Pay
terms.v: {pay} per month, paid at the end of the month

conditions: A copy of your passport or national ID.
Your signature on the rules, including confidentiality.
Every supplier, price, and order written in the company's order sheet, not only your notes.
Your first sample check, signed off by {manager}.
expect: No large order goes out before a sample passed the check.
The Head of Deployment hears that a date will slip before it slips.
The spare pool stays full: ten percent extra of every item.
offer.closing: Please sign below to accept this offer. We look forward to working with you.

handbook.purpose: Every accepted hour starts with a phone on a worker's head, on a mount, on a cap. Egypt cannot film without this gear, and cannot wait weeks when a site opens. You buy all of it in China, in large numbers, at a fair price, and you know where every order is.
outcomes: Every item Egypt orders arrives on the date you gave, in the count ordered.
No bad batch reaches a site. Every large order passed a sample first.
Ten percent spares of every item are always in stock.
Mazen and Ali Ateem hear about a problem the day you do.
daily: Morning. Open the order sheet. Ask each supplier if its open order is on time.
A sample lands. Check angle, comfort, how long it lasts, safety. Photos to Ali Ateem.
A date slips. Tell Mazen and Aly the same day, with the new date.
Before you sign. Price, count, date, and payment terms are written, and Aly said yes.
weekly: Once a week. The call with Aly: open orders, prices, samples, what Egypt needs next.
Once a week. Ask Mazen what the store is short of. Plan the next order.
monthly: Review the month's orders with Aly: late, failed, or cost more. Fix the cause.
standards: No large order without a sample that passed. A photo is not a sample.
Egypt plans on the date you give. Say the real date, not the hoped-for one.
Every payment goes through Ahmed Alaa against a record. Above the threshold, Adham signs second.
A supplier knows what we buy and nothing more. Never the client, never the footage.
Every order lands at the store in Cairo, never at a site.
never: Never take a gift, cut, or favor from a supplier. It ends the job.
Nobody contacts the client. Anything about the client goes to Adham.
Saying the client's name to anyone outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: With Aly. The item list, the standards, today's suppliers, and the order sheet.
Calls with Mazen and Ali Ateem. What Egypt needs, what a good mount looks like.
Your first sample check, from start to finish. Aly signs it off.
Your first order, placed and tracked. Aly reads every line before you sign.

measures: Orders that arrived on the date you gave, in the count ordered.
Batches that failed at the store after passing your sample. Zero.
Days the spare pool was under ten percent.
Price per unit for each item, month against month.
handbook.call: Aly, for everything. Mazen for what Egypt needs. Ali Ateem for a sample or a design. Mano for the store. Ahmed Alaa for a payment.
